PMID: 42996502



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nCIT) has emerged as a standard treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This study aimed to evaluate the independent prognostic value of postoperative pathological N stage (ypN) and to assess whether pre-treatment clinical N stage (cN) provides additional prognostic information in patients achieving ypN0. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 194 ESCC patients who received nCIT followed by radical esophagectomy between January 2019 and December 2024. Patients were stratified into three groups: cN0/ypN0 (n=104), cN+/ypN0 (n=32), and ypN+ (n=58). Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models were used for survival analysis. Multivariable models were constructed using a clinically informed variable-selection strategy constrained by the number of events. For the three pairwise comparisons, unadjusted P values were compared against a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold of alpha=0.017 (0.05/3). RESULTS: A total of 194 patients were enrolled, with 31 deaths and 37 recurrences during a median follow-up of 34.0 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier). ypN+ patients had significantly worse overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) than ypN- patients (both Log-rank P<0.001). In the primary multivariable model, ypN+ was an independent adverse prognostic factor for OS (HR = 3.204, 95%CI: 1.563-6.568, P = 0.001) and RFS (HR = 3.780, 95%CI: 1.943-7.356, P<0.001), and remained robust across extended, cycle-adjusted, and landmark sensitivity analyses. Among the three groups, ypN+ showed significantly shorter OS compared with both ypN0 groups (P = 0.002 vs cN0/ypN0; P = 0.008 vs cN+/ypN0; both below the Bonferroni threshold) and shorter RFS compared with cN0/ypN0 (P<0.001). No significant difference was observed between cN0/ypN0 and cN+/ypN0 groups for OS (P = 0.259); the RFS comparison was nominally significant but did not survive Bonferroni correction (HR = 2.799, 95%CI: 1.048-7.479, unadjusted P = 0.040). CONCLUSION: Postoperative ypN stage is the core prognostic determinant in ESCC after nCIT. In patients achieving ypN0, pre-treatment cN did not demonstrate statistically significant additional prognostic discrimination in this cohort, although estimates were imprecise due to the small cN+/ypN0 subgroup and limited events. Postoperative risk assessment should be based primarily on ypN status; these findings require validation in larger, preferably multicenter, cohorts.

item.title: Application of chimeric flaps for complex orbitomaxillary reconstruction in sinonasal malignancy.
item.dc:creator: Panchal K, Manikantan K, Samadder S, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu G
item.description:
Authors: Panchal K, Manikantan K, Samadder S, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1963043
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996499



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal malignancies are rare tumors, and a subset of these patients presents with involvement of the orbitomaxillary area, resulting in a complex maxillectomy defect, which warrants primary reconstruction. Complexity increases with globe preservation, which mandates structural support to the globe, ideally reconstructed using a vascularized osseous flap. Such complex defect reconstruction requires multiple components, which are titrated according to the complex three-dimensional defects. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the outcomes of primary orbitomaxillary reconstruction in sinonasal malignancy using multicomponent chimeric flaps, which included osseous chimeric flaps for globe-preserving total maxillectomy and soft tissue chimeric flaps for the remaining orbitomaxillary defects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and April 2026 at a tertiary referral center. The cohort included consecutive patients with modified Brown type 3 to 6 maxillectomy defects having sinonasal malignancy, which were primarily reconstructed with chimeric flaps. Data on the pathology, type of orbito maxillectomy defects, and types and components of chimeric flaps were collected. Outcomes were measured by flap survival, re-explorations, wound healing compromise, and delays in the start of adjuvant therapy. Specifically for orbital preservation patients, further assessment was made on the presence of diplopia or enophthalmos. RESULTS: All 11 patients included in the study underwent a chimeric flap for orbitomaxillary defects. The most common pathology was squamous cell carcinoma. Seven (64%) were soft tissue chimeric flaps, and four (36%) were osseous chimeric flaps. All flaps survived completely. Satisfactory wound healing and contour restoration were achieved in all patients. CONCLUSION: Chimeric flaps with their multiple components, which can be contoured according to the complex three-dimensional orbitomaxillary defects, achieves primary healing. For total maxillectomy with globe preservation, bone reconstruction is warranted. Orbital bone reconstruction use of 3D model for contouring the bone strut and the orbital floor mesh can achieve accurate reconstruction for such complex defects.

item.title: Outcomes of sequential microvascular tissue transfer for radiation induced sequelae post mandibular reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Panchal K, Ukil S, Kalwadia N, Samadder S, Manikantan K, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu GC
item.description:
Authors: Panchal K, Ukil S, Kalwadia N, Samadder S, Manikantan K, Arun P, Kekatpure VD, Jain PV, Sahu GC
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1897431
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42996241



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy-related complications following mandibular reconstruction remain a major challenge in head and neck oncologic reconstruction. Although free fibula flap reconstruction has become the gold standard for segmental mandibular defects, delayed radiation-induced sequelae such as hardware exposure, contour deformity, soft tissue atrophy, fistula formation continue to affect long-term outcomes. Literature regarding the role of sequential microvascular tissue transfer in managing these complications remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the indications, surgical planning, recipient vessel selection, and outcomes of sequential microvascular free tissue transfer performed for radiation-induced sequelae after mandibular reconstruction. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Patients who had previously undergone primary mandibular reconstruction using a fibula free flap followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and later developed radiation-related complications requiring secondary microvascular reconstruction were included. Demographic data, primary reconstructive details, radiation parameters, duration between radiation and complication, indications for sequential reconstruction, flap characteristics, recipient vessel selection, postoperative complications, and healing outcomes were analyzed. RESULTS: Ten patients were included in the study. All patients had undergone primary fibula free flap reconstruction following segmental mandibulectomy followed by sequential microvascular soft tissue reconstruction for radiation induced complications. Ipsilateral superficial temporal vessels were used as recipient vessels in all cases without using vein grafts. All flaps survived completely. Satisfactory wound healing and contour restoration were achieved in all patients. CONCLUSION: Sequential microvascular reconstruction represents a reliable and effective strategy for managing radiation-induced complications following mandibular reconstruction. Volume loss can be addressed during plate removal surgery which not only achieves a stable soft tissue cover but also prevents further progression to osteoradionecrosis.

item.title: The cervicovaginal microbiome as a candidate correlate and potential predictor of HPV clearance and treatment response after HSIL therapy: a scoping review.
item.dc:creator: Mwesige B, Angucia B, Mbodi L, Mwazha A, Niyonzima N, Mwansa-Kambafwile J, Breiman RF, Zakumumpa H, Chikandiwa A
item.description:
Authors: Mwesige B, Angucia B, Mbodi L, Mwazha A, Niyonzima N, Mwansa-Kambafwile J, Breiman RF, Zakumumpa H, Chikandiwa A
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1972845
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42991095



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection causes virtually all high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and cervical cancer, but only a minority progress, implicating host and microenvironmental cofactors. The cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM), particularly Lactobacillus-dominated communities, may influence hrHPV persistence, clearance, and response to HSIL treatment. OBJECTIVE: To map evidence linking the CVM with hrHPV clearance and outcomes after HSIL treatment, including loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) and conization, using PRISMA-ScR and Arksey and O'Malley frameworks. METHODS: Literature on cervicovaginal microbiota, community state types (CSTs), HPV natural history, HSIL/CIN treatment, probiotics, microbiome-directed interventions, and predictive biomarkers was systematically searched and narratively synthesized using a Population-Concept-Context framework. RESULTS: Sixty-six sources were charted. Lactobacillus crispatus-dominated communities (CST-I) were associated with hrHPV clearance and favorable post-treatment outcomes, whereas CST-IV, bacterial vaginosis, and increased alpha-diversity were associated with hrHPV persistence, greater HSIL severity, and treatment failure. Proposed mechanisms include lactic acid-mediated pH regulation, D-lactic acid signaling, and modulation of viral oncoproteins and immune responses. Excision altered the CVM, with restoration of Lactobacillus dominance accompanying viral clearance. Microbial-signature machine-learning models showed promising but preliminary predictive performance. Oral and intravaginal probiotics showed inconsistent but generally favorable trends, with strongest evidence for intravaginal L. crispatus transplantation. Gut microbiome diversity may also influence chemoradiotherapy outcomes in invasive cervical cancer. CONCLUSION: The CVM is a promising predictor of hrHPV clearance and HSIL treatment response. However, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, and limited prospective evidence restrict clinical translation. Large prospective studies and rigorously designed trials are needed to validate predictive signatures and determine whether microbiome profiling or targeted modulation can improve HSIL management and outcomes.

item.title: PF chemotherapy combined with a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody as first-line treatment in patients with recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a prospective, single-arm, phase II clinical study.
item.dc:creator: Liao W, Li Q, Deng Y, Zhang J, Zhao Y, Zhang S
item.description:
Authors: Liao W, Li Q, Deng Y, Zhang J, Zhao Y, Zhang S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1961360
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42990899



Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the antitumor activity and safety of cadonilimab, a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) bispecific antibody, combined with platinum/carboplatin and 5-fluorouracil (PF) chemotherapy as first-line treatment for patients with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC). METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm, phase II trial, patients with histopathologically confirmed R/M HNSCC received cadonilimab (10 mg/kg) plus PF chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4-6 cycles, followed by maintenance cadonilimab. The primary endpoint was 1-year progression-free survival (PFS). A target sample size of 30 was planned, but the study was terminated prematurely after enrolling 16 patients due to slow accrual. RESULTS: Sixteen patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 18.4 months (range, 4.6 - 39.6), the 1-year PFS and overall survival (OS) rates were 50.0% (95% CI: 30.6% - 81.6%) and 75.0% (95% CI: 56.5% - 99.5%), respectively. The Objective Response Rate (ORR) was 56.3% (95% CI: 29.9% - 80.2%). Median PFS and OS were 9.8 months (95% CI: 2.8 - NR) and 17.7 months (95% CI: 12.3 - NR), respectively. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in four patients (25%), with no treatment-related deaths or immune-related cardiac toxicities reported. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, first-line cadonilimab combined with PF chemotherapy exhibited potential antitumor activity and manageable safety profiles in patients with R/M HNSCC. Given the favorable baseline profile of the cohort and the single-arm design, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Larger randomized controlled trials are required to determine whether dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade offers an incremental benefit over standard anti-PD-1-based regimens.

item.title: AICAR induces S phase cell cycle arrest in ESCC by targeting the AMPK/mTORC1 and mTORC2/AKT pathway.
item.dc:creator: Zou M, Zhang T, He L, Li J, Lin Z, Jia C, Ma K, Wang L, Xu S, Cai B, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zou M, Zhang T, He L, Li J, Lin Z, Jia C, Ma K, Wang L, Xu S, Cai B, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1975805
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42990857



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: 5-Aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide-1-β-4-ribofuranoside (AICAR), an AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) agonist, exhibits potent antitumor capacity across various malignancies. However, its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remain largely unexplored. METHODS: We treated HEEC, TE1, and TE13 cells with AICAR and assessed proliferation, cell cycle distribution, and expression of key signaling proteins, followed by SN38 cotreatment to evaluate apoptosis and chemosensitization. RESULTS: AICAR treatment suppressed proliferation in all three cell lines but induced a distinct S-phase arrest specifically in ESCC cells. Mechanistically, AICAR activated AMPK, which concurrently inhibited the mTORC1 pathway via TSC2 phosphorylation and activated the mTORC2/AKT pathway through FOXO3-mediated transcriptional upregulation of Rictor. A critical difference was observed between cell types: in HEEC cells, AICAR treatment upregulated the tumor suppressor PTEN, which prevented full AKT activation. In contrast, ESCC cells, with unaltered PTEN and dysfunctional p53, sustained AKT hyperactivation. This drove cells into S-phase, where they were subsequently arrested due to the parallel inhibition of mTORC1. Furthermore, synchronizing ESCC cells in the S-phase with AICAR, followed by its withdrawal and subsequent treatment with SN38, significantly enhanced apoptosis. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal that AICAR induces S-phase arrest in ESCC cells by dually modulating the mTORC1 and mTORC2/AKT signaling pathways. This differential effect, stemmed from dysfunctional p53/PTEN axis in ESCC cells, distinguishes ESCC cells from normal epithelial cells. Together, these results suggest that AICAR synchronizes ESCC cells in the S phase, thereby sensitizing them to S-phase-specific agents like SN38 and representing a potential novel strategy for ESCC treatment.

item.title: Machine learning to predict osteoradionecrosis in head and neck cancer.
item.dc:creator: Castro VT, Dalmazo LMT, Reis PEDD, de Abreu WC, Dos Reis RG, Prado-Ribeiro AC, Leite AF, Almeida FT, Guerra ENS
item.description:
Authors: Castro VT, Dalmazo LMT, Reis PEDD, de Abreu WC, Dos Reis RG, Prado-Ribeiro AC, Leite AF, Almeida FT, Guerra ENS
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1955800
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42985507



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Osteoradionecrosis is one of the most severe late adverse effects of head and neck radiotherapy. Predictive models may help identify patients at increased risk and support personalized treatment. This exploratory study aimed to develop a machine learning-based prediction model for osteoradionecrosis in a real-world cohort, following the TRIPOD+AI statement. METHODS: Clinical variables and mandibular dose-volume histogram parameters were collected from head and neck cancer patients treated with radiotherapy. Forward Stepwise Logistic Regression was used for predictor selection. Six machine learning algorithms, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, CatBoost, XGBoost, and TabPFN, were evaluated under class-weighted baseline modelling, threshold optimization, and data augmentation with repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Performance was primarily assessed using sensitivity. Pairwise comparisons used the Nadeau-Bengio corrected paired t-test with Holm adjustment. RESULTS: Ninety-seven patients were included, of whom 8 developed osteoradionecrosis (8.25%). Of the 80 available variables, V60Gy and tumor location in the oral cavity were selected as predictors. Without augmentation, Logistic Regression achieved the highest sensitivity (0.74 [95% CI: 0.40-1.00]), while several algorithms showed poor sensitivity. With data augmentation, sensitivity ranged from 0.72 to 0.77 across models, with TabPFN, CatBoost, Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine reaching the highest sensitivity. Logistic Regression achieved the highest AUC under both strategies (0.87). However, F1 scores remained modest, reaching a maximum of 0.48. CONCLUSION: Machine learning models demonstrated exploratory potential for ORN risk assessment within an internal validation framework. Class-imbalance strategies were associated with greater minority-class detection in this cohort, but their generalizability remains uncertain. Larger multicenter cohorts and external validation are needed before clinical implementation.

item.title: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Y, Xiao H, Feng D, López-Huerta VG, Wang K, Xi K, Hartley ND, Arias-Garcia MA, Liu T, Wang W, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhou Y, Xiao H, Feng D, López-Huerta VG, Wang K, Xi K, Hartley ND, Arias-Garcia MA, Liu T, Wang W, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79022-6
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 43003851



Abstract:
Social preference in autism spectrum disorder varies across contexts, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Shank3 knockout (KO) mice, an autism mouse model, exhibit reduced preference for social over nonsocial stimuli while retaining a preference for females over males. Calcium imaging reveals context-dependent differences between KO and wild-type (WT) mice in the organization of neuronal population dynamics in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), corresponding to their behavioural preferences. Functional imaging and molecular analyses reveal reduced functional connectivity between the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and DMS and molecular alterations more pronounced in the striatal matrix. ACC inhibition eliminates genotype-dependent differences in DMS dynamics. Inhibiting the ACC-DMS pathway impairs social preference, whereas its activation in KO mice shifts DMS dynamics towards WT patterns and improves social preference. These findings identify a cortical pathway that shapes striatal population dynamics and context-dependent social preference in an autism mouse model.

item.title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice.
item.dc:creator: Yu Z, Abulipizi G, Fang Y, Qu C, Ding L, Zong Z, Huang J, Chen Z, Zhou J, Li Z, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Yu Z, Abulipizi G, Fang Y, Qu C, Ding L, Zong Z, Huang J, Chen Z, Zhou J, Li Z, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78675-7
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 43015315



Abstract:
Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

item.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease.
item.dc:creator: Zhang F, Chen L, Wang S, Chen X, Du K, Song F, Jiang L, Feng Y, Du S, Jiang T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhang F, Chen L, Wang S, Chen X, Du K, Song F, Jiang L, Feng Y, Du S, Jiang T, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78633-3
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 43009500



Abstract:
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEPTA-Ce, with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEPTA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEPTA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

item.title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda).
item.dc:creator: Funston GF, Dudgeon TW, Simon DJ, Dufault DM, Boyd C, Fowler D, Currie PJ, Evans DC
item.description:
Authors: Funston GF, Dudgeon TW, Simon DJ, Dufault DM, Boyd C, Fowler D, Currie PJ, Evans DC
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78343-w
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 43003810



Abstract:
The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi-the first for the clade-reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit-which shaped early Cenozoic flora-remains unclear.

item.title: Periodontal pathogen Tannerella forsythia promotes liver fibrosis via ICAM-1⁺ neutrophil-dependent hepatic stellate cell activation.
item.dc:creator: Tang D, Wei J, Liu M, Cui L, Chen J, Li H, Lin M, Li X, Ou Q, Li Q
item.description:
Authors: Tang D, Wei J, Liu M, Cui L, Chen J, Li H, Lin M, Li X, Ou Q, Li Q
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78008-8
Published: 2026-Oct-09
PMID: 42988798



Abstract:
Periodontitis is a key driver in the development and progression of liver fibrosis. Nevertheless, how specific periodontal pathogens contribute to liver fibrosis remains elusive. Here, we identify Tannerella forsythia as the crucial mediator in the link between periodontitis and liver fibrosis, which can translocate to the gut and aggravate liver fibrosis. Mechanistically, Tannerella forsythia promotes the infiltration of ICAM-1+ neutrophils and inflammatory response in the liver via disrupting intestinal barrier integrity. ICAM-1+ neutrophils secrete TNF-α, which activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway in hepatic stellate cells, triggering collagen deposition and fibrogenesis. Conditional knockout of ICAM-1 in neutrophils or global deletion of TNF-α significantly attenuates inflammatory response and liver fibrosis caused by Tannerella forsythia. Taken together, this study identifies an oral-gut-liver axis driven by Tannerella forsythia and provides a prospective therapeutic target for periodontitis-related liver fibrosis.

item.title: Risk factors for reoperation in patients hospitalized with odontogenic infection-a single center study.

Authors: Kaercher D, Schieren I, Thelen P, Li L, Hamprecht A, Ruettermann M
Journal: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oooo.2026.09.010
Published: 2026-Sep-22
PMID: 42998963



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Odontogenic infections are common in oral and maxillofacial surgery. In some patients, further surgical drainage is needed. This study evaluated risk factors for reoperation in hospitalised patients with odontogenic infections. STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective, single-centre cohort study was conducted in 1,173 hospitalised patients treated for odontogenic infections between January 2014 and April 2020. Patients were divided into a reoperation group (n = 38) and a no-reoperation group (n = 1,135). RESULTS: Chronic renal failure (OR: 5.985, 95% CI: 2.174-16.475; P < .001), chronic respiratory disease (OR: 2.51, 95% CI: 1.031-6.261; P = .043), parapharyngeal space involvement (OR: 4.09, 95% CI: 1.873-8.943; P < .001), and buccal space 1 involvement (OR: 3.431, 95% CI: 1.283-9.179; P = .014) were associated with reoperation in univariable analysis. Admission C-reactive protein was associated with reoperation, but the small dataset limits interpretation.

item.title: Prognostic significance of systemic inflammatory and peripheral immune profiles in differentiated thyroid carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Zhang X, Liu F, Wang W, Peng C, Qin Y
item.description:
Authors: Zhang X, Liu F, Wang W, Peng C, Qin Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16883-6
Published: 2026-Sep-04
PMID: 42995540



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) generally has a favorable prognosis, a subset of patients develop aggressive disease associated with poor outcomes. Current risk stratification relies mainly on clinicopathological features, whereas circulating inflammatory and immune biomarkers may provide complementary prognostic information. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of systemic inflammatory status, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune profiles in patients with DTC. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 430 patients with pathologically confirmed DTC who underwent surgical resection. Preoperative inflammatory markers, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune cell profiles were evaluated, and their associations with overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression models. RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls and patients with benign thyroid nodules, patients with DTC exhibited significantly elevated levels of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), thyroglobulin (Tg), and thyroglobulin antibody (TgAb) (all P < 0.001). Higher levels of SII, Tg, and TgAb were associated with lymph node metastasis and distant metastasis. Multivariable Cox regression analysis identified older age, follicular thyroid carcinoma, lymph node metastasis, distant metastasis, elevated SII, increased Tg and TgAb levels, and higher CD8⁺ T-cell proportion as independent predictors of inferior OS. Kaplan-Meier analyses further demonstrated that higher proportions of CD3+, CD4+, and CD19 + cells and lower proportions of CD56 + cells were associated with improved OS, whereas CD127 + cell proportion showed no significant association with OS. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic inflammatory status, thyroid-related biomarkers, and peripheral immune cell profiles provide complementary prognostic information in patients with DTC. Integration of SII, Tg/TgAb levels, and immune profiling may complement existing risk stratification approaches and facilitate individualized postoperative risk assessment and surveillance.

item.title: Role of CDC25B in human cancers: a meta-analysis and bioinformatics analysis.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: CDC25B, as an important member of the CDC25 family, plays a vital role in cell regulation. Recent studies have identified it as a potential oncogene implicated in tumorigenesis and cancer progression. The goal of our research was to shed light on the usefulness and significance of CDC25B as a reliable marker for predicting cancer outcomes. METHODS: The databases PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Wanfang data were used to find relevant articles published prior to May 30, 2025. The correlation between CDC25B expression and tumor prognosis or clinical features by calculating the overall hazard ratio or odds ratio and 95% confidence interval. To further verify our results, we also employed an online database from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and GTEx. RESULTS: Our study selected 16 articles for meta-analysis, including 2056 cancer patients. The current study showed that higher CDC25B expression was linked to poorer overall survival (OS) (HR =1.90, 95% CI: 1.45-2.48) and disease free survival (DFS) (HR =5.99, 95% CI: 1.07-33.63) in some cancers. Subgroups analysis indicated that CDC25B was significantly linked to poor OS in digestive system cancer, breast cancer and other tumors, but not related to repiratory system cancer. Correlation analysis demonstrated that CDC25B was linked to lymph node metastasis, T stage and TNM stage, not related to gender and clinical stage. Sensitive analysis indicated that the analysis of OS and T stage was stable. Begg's and Egger's tests indicated no publication bias in terms of gender, lymph node metastasis, T stage, and TNM stage. Bioinformatics analysis showed that CDC25B was over-expressed in most cancers. Cox regression found that CDC25B expression was linked to OS, DSS and PFI in ACC, KIRC, LIHC, and UVM. The frequency of CDC25B gene alteration was highest in OV. GSEA analysis demonstrated that CDC25B was invoved in apoptosis and cell cycle in most tumors. CDC25B was correlated with immnue cell infiltration in cancers. CONCLUSION: Abnormal CDC25B expression is linked to the clinical prognosis and pathological characteristics of different cancers. CDC25B expression levels are only associated with prognosis in specific cancer types (KIRC, LIHC, UVM).

item.title: A cfDNA fragmentomics-based liquid biopsy assay for early detection of oral cancer.
item.dc:creator: Wang W, Ding T, Liu C, Hong X, He P, Yang W, Zhong M, Jiang Y
item.description:
Authors: Wang W, Ding T, Liu C, Hong X, He P, Yang W, Zhong M, Jiang Y
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16606-x
Published: 2026-Aug-15
PMID: 43009804



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early detection of oral cancer improves outcomes, but remains limited by the invasiveness and low sensitivity of current screening methods. METHODS: This study included 342 participants (200 in the training and 142 in the validation cohorts). Plasma cfDNA underwent low-depth whole-genome sequencing, with data normalized to a standardized 5× coverage via down-sampling to ensure consistent analysis. Three cfDNA-derived features, including fragment size ratio (FSR), copy number variation (CNV), and repetitive element profiles (REP), were extracted and integrated using a stacked machine learning ensemble to generate prediction scores. Model performance was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: In the training cohort, oral cancer patients had a median age of 53 years (91% male), while healthy individuals had a median age of 57 years (37% male). In the validation cohort, the median ages were 53 and 57 years, with male proportions of 83.1% and 38.0% in the cancer and healthy groups, respectively. Cancer samples exhibited shorter cfDNA fragments, recurrent CNV gains at 3q and 8q, and losses at 3p and 5q. The individual AUCs for FSR, CNV, and REP were 0.973, 0.983, and 0.979 in the training cohort, and 0.960, 0.982, and 0.972 in the validation cohort, respectively. The integrated stacked model achieved AUCs of 0.996 (95% CI: 0.991-1.000) and 0.988 (95% CI: 0.975-0.988) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. To prioritize high specificity for large-scale screening, a decision threshold was established in the training cohort to target 98.0% specificity, which yielded a corresponding sensitivity of 98.0%. When this pre-fixed threshold was blindly applied to the independent validation cohort, a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 95.8% were achieved. Prediction scores were not significantly associated with age, sex, or tumor site. CONCLUSIONS: The cfDNA fragmentomics-based stacked model distinguished oral cancer from healthy individuals, including early stage disease, supporting its potential for noninvasive approach for oral cancer detection.

item.title: Microbial dysbiosis and treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events in locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an exploratory study of the oral and gut microbiome.
item.dc:creator: Chen Y, Huang C, Qin Y, Jian Y, Li L, Li J, Meng Z, Kang M
item.description:
Authors: Chen Y, Huang C, Qin Y, Jian Y, Li L, Li J, Meng Z, Kang M
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16631-w
Published: 2026-Aug-14
PMID: 43015659



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal adverse events are frequent during treatment for locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC) and can impair nutritional status and treatment tolerance. Radiotherapy and chemotherapy may disrupt microbial communities, but whether oral and gut microbiota are associated with treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events remains unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Oral swab and stool samples from 80 patients with LA-NPC were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Associations between treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events and oral microbial composition were evaluated, together with analyses of microbial functions and gut microbial profiles. Oral microbiota features were then used to develop machine learning models for distinguishing patients with gastrointestinal adverse events. RESULTS: Among 80 patients with LA-NPC, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation occurred in 72.5%, 51.3%, 46.3%, and 67.5%, respectively. Oral microbiota analysis showed enrichment of Alloprevotella, Fusobacterium, and Campylobacter in patients with gastrointestinal adverse events or a high symptom burden, whereas Rothia and Streptococcus were enriched in those without events or with a low burden. Predicted oral microbial functions involved propanoate metabolism, lipoic acid metabolism, retinol metabolism, glycan degradation, sphingolipid metabolism, calcium signaling, and lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis. Alterations in specific gut genera, including Helicobacter, Parasutterella, and Anaerotruncus, were also observed. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified oral and gut microbial features associated with treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events in patients with LA-NPC. Oral microbial features showed potential value for classifying gastrointestinal adverse event status during treatment.

item.title: Pre-treatment serum bicarbonate predicts survival in patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma undergoing definitive radiotherapy: a retrospective propensity score matching study.
item.dc:creator: Ji H, Zhang P, Wang Y, Su Y, Si H, Jia Y, Qiao X, Zhou Z
item.description:
Authors: Ji H, Zhang P, Wang Y, Su Y, Si H, Jia Y, Qiao X, Zhou Z
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16723-7
Published: 2026-Aug-14
PMID: 43009855



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of pre-treatment serum bicarbonate (HCO3-) for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC) patients undergoing definitive radiotherapy. METHODS: Patients with stage Ⅱ-Ⅳa ESCC treated with definitive radiotherapy between 2015 and 2022 were screened and then divided into Group A (high HCO3-) and Group B (low HCO3-). Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using sex, age, ECOG score, body mass index, tumor length, tumor location, clinical T category, clinical N category, clinical TNM stage, combined chemotherapy, and radiation dose as covariates at a 1:2 ratio (Group A: Group B). OS and PFS were compared between different groups using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: A total of 301 patients were included in the study. The median follow-up time was 54.1 months. The median OS and PFS were 17.3 months and 11.0 months. The median HCO3- was 24.9 mmol/L. Before PSM, the median OS was 27.0 months in Group A (HCO3- ≥26 mmol/L, n = 103) and 14.8 months in Group B (HCO3- <26 mmol/L, n = 198), p < 0.0001. The median PFS was 16.3 months in Group A and 9.6 months in Group B, p = 0.0002. After 1:2 PSM, the median OS was 25.7 months in Group A (n = 97) and 15.3 months in Group B (n = 169), p = 0.0011. The median PFS was 13.0 months in Group A and 9.6 months in Group B, p = 0.0059. Multivariate Cox analysis suggested that age ≥ 66 (HR 0.739, p = 0.036), T category < 3 (HR 0.484, p < 0.001), clinical N category < 2 (HR 0.713, p = 0.022), combined chemotherapy (HR 0.625, p = 0.003), and HCO3- ≥26 mmol/L (HR 0.656, p = 0.004) were independent favorable prognostic factors for OS. Clinical T category < 3 (HR 0.565, p < 0.001), clinical stage Ⅱ-Ⅲ (HR 0.685, p = 0.019), and pre-treatment HCO3- ≥26 mmol/L (HR 0.717, p = 0.019) were independent favorable prognostic factors for PFS. CONCLUSIONS: A high pre-treatment serum bicarbonate level is associated with an increased OS and PFS in LA-ESCC patients undergoing definitive radiotherapy. Therefore, pre-treatment serum bicarbonate may serve as a readily available prognostic biomarker to inform risk stratification and treatment planning in LA-ESCC patients undergoing definitive radiotherapy.

item.title: Assessing the feasibility of uTPS for volumetric modulated arc therapy treatment plan optimization of dual-layer multileaf collimator linear accelerators.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual-layer multileaf collimator (MLC) accelerators, such as Halcyon, are increasingly used in clinical settings; however, the ability of treatment planning systems (TPS) to effectively optimize treatment plans for such accelerators remains an important consideration. PURPOSE: This study evaluates the feasibility of using uTPS to optimize treatment plans for dual-layer MLC accelerators, with Eclipse as a clinical reference. METHODS: Standard radiation data from the Halcyon 2.0 accelerator were used to model the beam in the uTPS (Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare Co., Ltd., version R001). Twenty cases were selected, with five each for hypopharyngeal, esophageal, breast, and cervical cancers. Volumetric modulated arc therapy plans were generated using the uTPS stochastic platform optimizer and the Eclipse photon optimizer (PO). All plans were calculated using the Acuros external beam (AXB) algorithm for dosimetric comparison. Key indicators, such as the conformity index (CI), homogeneity index (HI), and organ-at-risk (OAR) doses, were analyzed and compared. The feasibility of delivering uTPS plans on the Halcyon accelerator was validated. The dosimetric accuracy was confirmed using ArcCheck, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction were performed. RESULTS: uTPS and Eclipse plans exhibited similar dosimetric qualities for esophageal and cervical cancer cases, with no significant differences in CI, HI, and OAR doses. However, uTPS demonstrated superior OAR sparing in specific cases: in hypopharyngeal cancer, uTPS significantly reduced the brainstem [Formula: see text] by 34.48%, the left parotid[Formula: see text] by 11.8%, and the left parotid [Formula: see text] by 6.9% (all P < 0.05); in breast cancer, uTPS significantly reduced the spinal cord [Formula: see text]by 49.6% (P < 0.05). No statistically significant differences were observed in other dosimetric parameters. No significant differences in total monitor units were observed between the uTPS and Eclipse plans. item.title: Prognostic evaluation of stage I-IVa nasopharyngeal carcinoma: integrating PET/CT parameters, inflammatory and clinical features.

item.description:
Authors: Lv Y, Zheng D, Zhou Z, Dai Z, Wei S, Lan X, Gao Z, Qin C
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16679-8
Published: 2026-Aug-12
PMID: 43015633



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate prognostic 18F-FDG PET/CT parameters and develop a nomogram integrating inflammatory markers and clinicopathological characteristics for predicting progression-free survival (PFS) in stage I-IVa nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: Stage I-IVa NPC patients who underwent pretreatment 18F-FDG PET/CT were retrospectively collected. The 18F-FDG PET and clinicopathologic parameters were analyzed. The correlation among PET parameters was evaluated with Spearman's rho test. ROC curve was used to evaluate the predictive performance and calculate the optimal cut-off values for grouping. The survival analyses were performed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank test. Prognostic factors were identified using Cox regression, and a nomogram was constructed and validated. RESULTS: Eighty‑six patients were enrolled (63 [73.26%] males, mean age 48.38 ± 11.91 years). Heterogeneity factor (HF) and metabolic tumor volume (MTV) showed strong correlation (r = 0.88, P < 0.01). ROC curve analysis indicated HF and MTV exhibited good predictive value for 1-, 3-, and 5-year PFS (HF: AUC = 0.817, 0.678, and 0.672; MTV: AUC = 0.866, 0.685, and 0.670), with the best prognostic efficacy for 1-year PFS. HF, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), overall stage, and concurrent chemoradiotherapy were independent predictors of 5-year PFS. The nomogram demonstrated high predictive ability for PFS, with AUCs of 0.83-0.86 and a C-index of 0.78, further supported by its clinical utility. CONCLUSION: The novel multifactor nomogram combining HF with SII, overall stage, and treatment strategy (concurrent chemoradiotherapy) demonstrates superior prognostic predictive performance, improving accuracy and enabling personalized assessment in I-IVa stage NPC patients management.

item.title: Integrated genomic analysis of tumor mutational burden reveals heterogeneous immunotherapy outcomes in head and neck cancer.
item.dc:creator: Chen Y, Han T, Xi X, Chen D, Zhang Q, Zhang X, Lei Z
item.description:
Authors: Chen Y, Han T, Xi X, Chen D, Zhang Q, Zhang X, Lei Z
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16012-3
Published: 2026-Aug-12
PMID: 43009817



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck cancer (HNC) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy. Immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the treatment landscape of head and neck cancer; however, substantial heterogeneity in clinical outcomes remains. Tumor mutational burden (TMB) is widely reported in clinical sequencing assays; however, its standalone value in guiding the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains inconsistent, and its interpretation alongside co-occurring genomic alterations is not well defined in routine practice. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 389 Chinese patients with HNC using a 551-gene targeted sequencing panel and validated key findings in the MSKCC ICI-treated cohort. Tumor mutational burden (TMB), copy number variation (CNV), tumor fusion burden (TFB), and germline variants were comprehensively profiled to identify molecular determinants of immunotherapy efficacy. RESULTS: TMB-high (TMB-H, ≥ 10 mut/Mb) tumors accounted for 23% of cases and were enriched for mutations in TP53, NOTCH1, and PIK3CA, whereas TMB-low (TMB-L) tumors showed frequent CNVs, including CCND1, EGFR, and FGFR1 amplifications and CDKN2A loss. In the MSKCC cohort, integrating TMB with the mutation status of PIK3CA, TP53, NOTCH1, and FAT1 provided improved stratification of immunotherapy outcomes compared with TMB alone, highlighting the importance of genomic context when interpreting mutation burden. Additionally, higher tumor fusion burden (TFB) correlated with distinct chemosensitivity patterns, and germline variants in DNA repair genes were associated with increased somatic mutation accumulation. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that immunotherapy outcomes in head and neck cancer are strongly influenced by the genomic context of tumor mutational burden. Integrated genomic analysis provides a biologically grounded framework for understanding heterogeneity in genomic-guided cancer treatment.

item.title: Geriatric nutritional risk index and prognosis in middle-aged and elderly patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yang Y, Liu W, Xu Y, Peng X, Lan Q, Luo Y, Huang L, Zeng Z
item.description:
Authors: Yang Y, Liu W, Xu Y, Peng X, Lan Q, Luo Y, Huang L, Zeng Z
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16722-8
Published: 2026-Aug-11
PMID: 43004250



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic value of the pretreatment Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) in middle-aged and older patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: This study included 235 patients with NPC aged ≥ 50 years. Patients were stratified into low GNRI (GNRI ≤ 98) and high GNRI (GNRI > 98) groups. The clinical characteristics were compared using the chi-square test. Survival outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves, log-rank tests, and Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Of the 235 patients included in the study, 110 (46.8%) were in the low GNRI group. During a median follow-up of 70 months, patients in the high GNRI group had significantly better overall survival (OS) and event-free survival (EFS) than those with (p < 0.05). Lower body mass index and serum albumin levels were independently associated with low GNRI. Multivariate analysis confirmed that low GNRI was an independent predictor of poorer OS (HR = 1.802, 95% CI: 1.122-2.894, p = 0.015) and EFS (HR = 1.694, 95% CI: 1.080-2.657, p = 0.022). No significant interactions were observed between GNRI and other variables (p > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Pretreatment GNRI independently predicts survival in middle-aged and elderly patients with NPC. A low GNRI identifies patients at higher risk of poor outcomes and may help guide prognostic evaluations and supportive care strategies.

item.title: Financial toxicity in patients with head and neck cancer: a scoping review.
item.dc:creator: E Silva DKV, da Silva RO, Silva SVA, Raymundo MLB, Monteiro DLA, Lucena WGL, Cavalcanti YW
item.description:
Authors: E Silva DKV, da Silva RO, Silva SVA, Raymundo MLB, Monteiro DLA, Lucena WGL, Cavalcanti YW
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16700-0
Published: 2026-Aug-11
PMID: 43000311



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Financial toxicity has emerged as an important outcome in oncology, particularly in head and neck cancer, due to therapeutic complexity and prolonged functional consequences. This study aimed to map and synthesize the available evidence on financial toxicity in patients with head and neck cancer. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science. After screening 1,466 studies, 29 met the eligibility criteria. Data were extracted by four reviewers, organized into a thematic matrix, and complemented by a bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer software. RESULTS: The studies, published between 2012 and 2025, showed that financial toxicity is frequent and multidimensional, involving direct costs (transportation, medications, food, and dental care related to oncological treatment) and indirect costs (loss of income and work absence). Factors such as low income, low educational level, informal employment, lack of insurance, and greater distance from treatment centers were associated with a higher risk of financial toxicity. This condition was associated with poorer quality of life, emotional distress, depressive symptoms, anxiety, treatment interruption or delay, and difficulties in returning to work. The most commonly used instrument was FACIT-COST, followed by FIT and author-developed questionnaires. Bibliometric analysis showed a concentration of studies in high-income countries and highlighted conceptual axes centered on "financial toxicity," "quality of life," and "treatment costs". CONCLUSION: Financial toxicity represents a relevant and multidimensional outcome in the care of patients with head and neck cancer, with important psychosocial implications. Its impacts are significant along the therapeutic trajectory and on quality of life, making its systematic inclusion in clinical assessment essential. There is a need to strengthen support systems and health policies that integrate financial, social, and psychological support, aiming to reduce inequalities and promote equity in access to oncological care.

item.title: Understanding HPV vaccination communication needs of parents of Turkish and Moroccan origin living in the Netherlands: a qualitative study.
item.dc:creator: Çayci E, Broek TVD, Nieboer AP
item.description:
Authors: Çayci E, Broek TVD, Nieboer AP
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28910-z
Published: 2026-Aug-11
PMID: 43000293



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: HPV vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, yet coverage in Europe remains low. In the Netherlands, uptake is particularly low among Turkish- and Moroccan-origin children, whose parents often have reservations about HPV vaccination, including mistrust, fear of side effects, and perceived information gaps. Understanding parents' preferences and expectations regarding HPV vaccination communication is essential for developing tailored strategies that support informed decision-making about children's vaccination. METHODS: We conducted 30 semi-structured interviews with Turkish- and Moroccan-origin parents of children aged 7-9 years in the Netherlands between April 2024 and January 2025. Interviews were conducted in Dutch or Turkish, with informal Tamazight translation when needed. RESULTS: Thematic analysis revealed a multidimensional discrepancy between official HPV vaccination information provision and parental expectations. Misalignment was perceived regarding communication setting, tone and framing of message, timing of information and messenger characteristics, which prompted some parents to rely on social networks and online sources. Parents suggested improvements, including timely, transparent and culturally sensitive communication delivered by trusted messengers familiar with their community. CONCLUSION: These findings underscore that effective HPV vaccination communication requires more than accurate information. Strategies must foster trust, engagement and comprehension, tailored to parental preferences. Tailoring content, formats, and sources to parental preferences may help reduce disparities in HPV vaccination uptake and support national and European immunization goals.

item.title: SLC3A2 identified as a new therapeutic target for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Li R, Cao S, Liu X, Zhao L, Gong C, Liu F, Qiu J, Wu C, Zhao M, Luo J
item.description:
Authors: Li R, Cao S, Liu X, Zhao L, Gong C, Liu F, Qiu J, Wu C, Zhao M, Luo J
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16448-7
Published: 2026-Aug-11
PMID: 42995537



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC), which is the most common malignant tumor of head and neck region. Programmed cell death pathways, including the ferroptosis pathway and the disulphide cell apoptotic pathway, have received increasing amounts of attention as potential targets for cancer therapy. However, the features of genes related to disulfidptosis and ferroptosis in HNSCC remain to be investigated. METHODS: We used a random survival forest (RSF) algorithm model, prognostic and immunological effects to screen SLC3A2. Drug sensitivity prediction and single-cell RNA-seq data further confirmed SLC3A2 as a therapeutic target. In addition, we validated SLC3A2 as a therapeutic target for HNSCC through in vitro experiments. RESULTS: In this study, we used TCGA and GEO database from multiple HNSCC cohorts to identify genes associated with disulphide-related cell death. The prognostic and immunological roles of these genes were investigated, and the key gene related to disulfidoptosis and ferroptosis, SLC3A2, was screened. Drug sensitivity prediction and single-cell RNA-seq data both indicate that SLC3A2 is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of HNSCC. Furthermore, our experiments suggest that overexpression of SLC3A2 in the absence of glucose suppress growth of HNSCC. We also found that knock down SLC3A2 could induce growth defects. In addition, we treated cells with a RING1B inhibitor to regulate SLC3A2 mRNA expression, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target in HNSCC. CONCLUSION: These findings suggested that SLC3A2 is a critical target in HNSCC development, providing new targets and research ideas for the treatment of HNSCC.

item.title: Screen-detected health conditions among students in grade 1-9: findings from Timor-Leste's first nationwide school-based screening program.
item.dc:creator: Jin H, Soares RM, Dos Reis Belo J, Soares F, Rosa AS, Mathur A, Cho M
item.description:
Authors: Jin H, Soares RM, Dos Reis Belo J, Soares F, Rosa AS, Mathur A, Cho M
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28730-1
Published: 2026-Aug-11
PMID: 42989189



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systematic health data on school-aged children in Timor-Leste have been lacking. The School-Based Primary Health Care Package screened students in Grade 1-9 nationwide in 2025. We describe the conditions detected and assess how far the estimates reflect variation between screeners. METHODS: Programmatic cross-sectional screening analysis of school-level records for 1,387 basic-education schools. Each community health center fielded at least one team consisting of one doctor and two nurses; the doctor performed physical examinations and substance-use assessments and nurses conducted anthropometry, vision and hearing assessments. Findings came from clinical examination or threshold-based tests, none confirmed by a reference standard, and are reported as screen-detected prevalence using assessment-specific denominator. Intracluster correlations and design effects were estimated directly and used for design-based confidence intervals. Inter-screener reliability was assessed by variance-components analysis across the 72 teams, benchmarked against nutritional status, the least judgement-dependent domain. RESULTS: Two hundred sixty-two thousand, four hundred thirty-four students were screened across 1,371 of 1,387 schools. Screen-detected dental caries affected 78,643 students (30.0%; design-based 95% CI 29.0-31.0), low BMI-for-age 53,565 (20.5%) and poor oral hygiene 44,508 (17.0%). Within-school clustering was strong, and municipal effect sizes were negligible after design correction (Cramér's V 0.012-0.028). Between-team variation was concentrated in the dental assessments, performed by the doctors: these showed a mean team effect 3.51 times the instrument-measured benchmark, versus 0.67 for the doctor's seven non-dental assessments (Mann-Whitney p = 0.012). Screen-detected caries ranged from 3.7% to 67.9% across 72 teams, and the screening team explained 43% of referral variance versus 13% for municipality. CONCLUSIONS: Dental caries and low BMI-for-age were the most frequently screen-detected problems. For the dental assessments the screening team accounted for more of the variation than the municipality, and this variation was specific to the dental tasks rather than to the examiners, who were consistent on assessments within their training. Screen-detected caries should be regarded as a lower bound and its municipal pattern not interpreted. Priorities are to calibrate the screening instrument, estimate caries prevalence through a pathfinder survey, and strengthen both preventive and restorative services.

item.title: Serum anti-POTEE antibodies as a novel serological biomarker for early detection and prognostic stratification in gastrointestinal cancers.
item.dc:creator: Sumazaki M, Yajima S, Ito M, Suzuki T, Oshima Y, Shiratori F, Takizawa H, Li SY, Zhang BS, Yoshida Y, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Sumazaki M, Yajima S, Ito M, Suzuki T, Oshima Y, Shiratori F, Takizawa H, Li SY, Zhang BS, Yoshida Y, et al.
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16732-6
Published: 2026-Aug-10
PMID: 43004301



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given the highly aggressive nature of gastrointestinal cancers, the identification of novel biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis is of considerable clinical importance. METHODS: Candidate cancer-testis (CT) antigens were first screened using RNA-sequencing data from normal human tissues; candidates showing high commonality across tumor RNA-sequencing datasets publicly available in The Cancer Genome Atlas were subsequently prioritized, and POTEE was identified as a promising target. Recombinant POTEE protein was expressed in Escherichia coli, purified by affinity chromatography, and used as the antigen for serological analysis. RESULTS: Serum levels of anti-POTEE antibodies (s-POTEE-Abs) were significantly elevated in 121 patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, 62 patients with gastric adenocarcinoma, and 158 patients with colorectal adenocarcinoma compared with those in 96 healthy donors. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis showed that the diagnostic performance of s-POTEE-Ab was comparable to that of s-p53-Ab, with area under the curve values of 0.832 versus 0.829 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, 0.680 versus 0.698 in gastric adenocarcinoma, and 0.735 versus 0.706 in colorectal adenocarcinoma, respectively. After multivariable adjustment, an independent prognostic association was retained only in CRAC. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that s-POTEE-Ab may represent a promising exploratory serological biomarker for gastrointestinal cancers. Its prognostic relevance appears to be cancer-type dependent and requires further validation in independent cohorts.

item.title: DLGAP1-AS2 knockdown increases chemosensitivity to vandetanib and synergistically inhibits metastatic activity of papillary thyroid cancer cells: experimental and computational approaches.
item.dc:creator: Oskuie SS, Mahdavi SZB, Nikravesh A, Baradaran B, Yari AH, Pourbagherian O, Mokhtarzadeh AA, Oroojalian F
item.description:
Authors: Oskuie SS, Mahdavi SZB, Nikravesh A, Baradaran B, Yari AH, Pourbagherian O, Mokhtarzadeh AA, Oroojalian F
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16511-3
Published: 2026-Aug-07
PMID: 42989125



Abstract:
Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) progression is closely associated with the regulatory roles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). The role of DLGAP1-AS2 has been investigated as a potentially oncogenic lncRNA (oncoLnc) in several malignancies; nevertheless, its specific tumorigenic activity in PTC remains largely unexplored.The relative expression of DLGAP1-AS2 was evaluated using FASTQ files and read count data obtained from thyroid cancer (THCA) samples accessible via the SRA and TCGA repositories. Additionally, siRNA transfection was employed to efficiently inhibit DLGAP1-AS2 activity. The effects of DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib on the proliferation and metastatic capability of PTC cells were evaluated using in vitro experiments (MTT, apoptosis analysis, DAPI staining, cell cycle assessment, and scratch & colony formation assays). The gene expressions of Caspase-3, Caspase-9, Bcl2, Bax, p53, CDK1, MMP-3, MMP-9, CD44, and CD133, WNT9B, MAPK10, and CACNA1D were determined using quantitative real-time PCR.Transfection with si-DLGAP1-AS2 resulted in a marked downregulation of DLGAP1-AS2 expression in B-CPAP cells. Treatment with si-DLGAP1-AS2 or vandetanib alone exerted limited effects on B-CPAP cells' viability, whereas their combination exerted marked toxicity against these cells and decreased the IC50 of vandetanib from 44.96 µg/ml to 27.36 µg/ml, reflecting the higher sensitivity of B-CPAP cells to this chemotherapeutic when combined with si-DLGAP1-AS2. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated that the combination therapy substantially augmented apoptosis rate, surpassing the level observed in si-DLGAP1-AS2 or vandetanib-treated groups. The sub-G1 cell population increased after si-DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib individual treatments, yet combination treatment led to a higher sub-G1 ratio. The combined use of si-DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib markedly impeded cell migration, accompanied by MMP-9 and MMP-3 downregulation. There was a down-expression of stemness-associated markers of CD44 and CD133 measured by qRT-PCR. Pro-apoptotic genes, including Caspase-3, Caspase-9 and Bax, were upregulated while Bcl2, WNT9B, MAPK10, and CACNA1D genes were substantially downregulated in the combined treatment group vs. control group. In conclusion, si-DLGAP1-AS2 and vandetanib combination promoted cell cycle arrest by regulating key genes involved in the process. DLGAP1-AS2 seems to be a potential prognostic biomarker involved in the molecular pathogenesis of PTC and a promising candidate for targeted therapy development.

item.title: Tumor budding and tumor-associated lymphocytic response as histopathological indicators of high-risk disease in head and neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Aksu D, Yalçın GŞ, Karasu N, Kuzu S, Özdemir Ç, Aksu U
item.description:
Authors: Aksu D, Yalçın GŞ, Karasu N, Kuzu S, Özdemir Ç, Aksu U
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16653-4
Published: 2026-Aug-04
PMID: 42983664



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tumor budding (TB) and tumor-associated lymphocytic response (TALR) have emerged as promising histopathological indicators of tumor aggressiveness across epithelial malignancies. Recent studies have suggested that both tumor invasive activity and host immune response contribute substantially to disease progression in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). However, data evaluating their combined significance in head and neck cSCC remain limited. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 187 primary head and neck cSCC cases was analyzed. TB was graded using a three-tier system, and TALR was categorized into three inflammatory response patterns. Associations with clinicopathological characteristics were evaluated using univariate analyses. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with high-risk disease, defined as advanced pathological stage (T3-T4). RESULTS: High-grade TB was significantly associated with adverse histopathological characteristics, including poor differentiation, increased depth of invasion, aggressive invasion pattern, perineural invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and advanced pathological stage (all p < 0.001). Weak TALR was associated with infiltrative growth characteristics and older age. In multivariable analysis, Grade 3 TB (OR 6.75, 95% CI 2.33-19.57), tumor depth > 6 mm (OR 4.03, 95% CI 2.03-8.38), poor differentiation (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.06-6.61), aggressive invasion pattern (OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.43-6.60), and weak TALR (OR 2.29, 95% CI 1.12-4.69) remained independently associated with high-risk disease. CONCLUSIONS: Tumor budding and tumor-associated lymphocytic response were independently associated with histopathological features of high-risk disease in head and neck cSCC. Their combined assessment may provide additional information for pathological risk stratification and may support incorporation into routine histopathological evaluation. Prospective studies incorporating recurrence and survival outcomes are required before definitive prognostic conclusions can be established.
